about.title: About Miniworld
about.intro: Miniworld is a living model of world history. Travel through time and fly around the Earth to see how the world changed.
about.simplification.climate: The colours of the land follow a rough climate pattern that changes with the ice age. Deserts follow how much rain fell, as worked out by scientists with a climate model, so they grow and shrink over time. The Sahara was green from about 12,800 to 3000 BCE; climate models miss most of that rain, so this green phase is added from what lake and pollen records show, and its dates are approximate. Real forests, deserts and grasslands were more varied.
about.simplification.land: The land is shaped as it is today. In the ice age, the heavy ice pressed the land down, and it slowly rose again afterwards. That is not shown.
about.simplification.lakes: Lakes that no longer exist, like the huge Lake Agassiz in North America, are not shown. The Black Sea, the Caspian Sea and the Baltic Sea are always shown full of water, even when the ocean was too low to reach them.
about.simplification.ice: The ice sheets come from a scientific reconstruction that shows them every 2,500 years. Between those steps the ice grows and melts evenly, and small glaciers are left out. Only where the ice was is shown, not how thick it was: every ice sheet is drawn as the same kind of smooth dome, without the land under it. The sea ice on the Arctic Ocean is drawn with a simple, made-up edge.
